input: Unfortunately, it has come to light that the outstanding equipment package is now expected to arrive some 3 weeks later than originally planned. According to the supplier, this delay has arisen as a result of a backlog that has built up within its own production schedule, which is, of course, outside our direct control. The implications of this are being carefully assessed; at this stage, it appears that design work will not be affected, and the main impact will be felt in the installation sequence, where setting and alignment activities will need to be revisited. As a mitigation, it is proposed that the installation work be resequenced so that packages already delivered to site are installed first, with the delayed package being taken out of the critical sequence until such time as it arrives. The procurement manager will take ownership of this resequencing exercise and of securing a revised delivery commitment from the supplier. The project board is asked to note this position, and to be aware that the resequencing will result in a considerably more compressed setting sequence at a later stage, which may in turn place additional pressure on
target: The outstanding equipment package will arrive 3 weeks late, and the supplier attributes the delay to a backlog in its own production schedule. The slip reaches the installation sequence rather than design: the drawings and the foundation work for this package are complete, so what moves is the start of setting and alignment, and the trades that follow the package move with it. One mitigation is available. The installation work can be resequenced so that the packages already on site are set first, and the delayed package is taken out of the critical sequence until it arrives; the procurement manager owns the resequencing and the revised delivery commitment from the supplier. The cost of the mitigation is a compressed setting sequence later, when the delayed package and the package behind it are handled in the same window and the labour for the two competes.
